subject: DataSprout integration — questions on private egress, mTLS, and structured output
messages:
From: Samira Khan <skhan@datasprout.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up — Redwood integration questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the call this morning — good intro. A couple of follow-ups from our platform team so we can scope next steps on the POC:

- Private networking: we need clarity on options for VPC endpoint vs. egress through our NAT. Can Redwood accept traffic via a VPC endpoint, or do you recommend IP allowlist + NAT egress?
- IP allowlists: if we go with IP allowlisting, can you provide the static IPs (or ranges) and SLAs around availability? Also, how often do those change with scale?
- DNS & egress: will DNS resolution for model endpoints happen within our VPC or by Redwood? Any requirements for outbound DNS (e.g., must allow redwood-internal domains)?
- mTLS: we need mutual TLS for the control-plane and optional client certs for data-plane. What cert formats do you accept and do you support automated rotation?
- SDK/auth: we plan to use the Redwood SDK from our backend (Node). Is the recommended auth model API key in a vault, or do you support signed JWTs / workload identity?
- Structured output & tool-calling: our product will call an internal service when the model returns an action payload. Can we rely on the streaming structured output option and are there examples for schema enforcement on Redwood responses?
- Embeddings & reranker: for document search we plan to embed content and run a reranker. Can you confirm embedding size limits, batching guidance, and if the reranker can be pinned to a model variant for consistency?

Were hoping to get a short tech-session next week with one of your engineers to confirm the VPC + cert details and to validate a minimal flow (SDK auth -> request -> structured response -> call internal tool).

Thanks,
Samira
VP Product, DataSprout

--
DataSprout Solutions

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <skhan@datasprout.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-15T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DataSprout integration — questions on private egress, mTLS, and structured output

Hi Samira,

Great to meet earlier — appreciate the clear list. Below is a concise recap and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned. Ill loop in Marissa (AE) and Ben (Solutions) to run the deep technical session.

Recap of options & short answers (details/links attached):
- VPC endpoint vs IP allowlist: Redwood supports both. For the tightest isolation we recommend a Private VPC Endpoint (we provide a managed interface endpoint). IP allowlisting is supported as a fallback; static ranges are available for Dedicated/Private tiers.
- IP ranges: in Private mode we can provide fixed /28 ranges per customer. For hosted customers we publish a stable set of egress IPs that change rarely; we'll include a signed IP list in the attachment.
- DNS & egress: If you use Private VPC Endpoint, DNS for redwood.internal endpoints resolves within your VPC (we provide conditional forwarding guidance). If you egress via NAT, allow outbound DNS to *.redwood.cloud and the usual certificate verification endpoints.
- mTLS: We support x509 PEM chains, mTLS for both control and data planes. Auto-rotation can be enabled via our KMS/HSM integrations (we can also accept customer-rotated cert bundles).
- SDK & auth: recommended is short-lived API tokens injected from your vault. We also support workload-identity (OIDC) and signed JWTs for Private deployments.
- Structured output & tool-calling: streaming structured output with schema enforcement is supported; we have a sample Node SDK flow that validates responses against a JSON Schema and triggers a webhook on action tokens.
- Embeddings & reranker: embeddings accept up to 8k tokens per batch; batching recommendations and tuner suggestions are in the attached checklist. Rerankers can be pinned to model variants with rollout policies.

Attachments: redwood-private-connectivity-checklist.pdf (contains IP ranges, DNS instructions, and cert formats)
Drive: datasprout-proposed-arch.png (customer-supplied arch we reviewed)
HubSpot: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/DS-2027-089

Proposed next steps / owners:
1) Technical deep-dive (60 min) to validate VPC endpoint and cert flow — proposed attendees: Ben (solutions), Karthik (infra), Samira + DataSprout infra team. (Action: Marissa to schedule)
2) Provide IP lists and sample Terraform for VPC endpoint setup (Action: Karthik by EOD Aug 16)
3) Share Node SDK example for streaming structured output + schema validation (Action: Ben by Aug 17)
4) Decide auth model (API keys vs OIDC) and share vault integration checklist (Action: DataSprout + Redwood)

Ill send calendar options shortly. Thanks again, and well make sure the deep-dive covers the exact cert formats and rotation cadence.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference

Hi Samira,

Looping in Ben to lead the tech session. A few clarifications from our side before we lock the session so we can prepare hands-on artifacts:

- VPC endpoint model: does DataSprout prefer an interface endpoint (AWS ENI-based) or a private link style proxy? If you have a VPC peer pattern already we can adapt. If you confirm ENI/interface, well provide Terraform snippets for the endpoint + security groups.
- IP allowlisting: are you looking for single primary range for the POC, or per-environment ranges (dev/staging/prod)? We can provide per-environment ranges if you sign up for Private tier or Dedicated; hosted will get shared ranges.
- mTLS keys: for POC we accept PEM bundles. For production do you plan to use customer-managed KMS for rotation or want Redwood to manage rotation? Both supported but the integration work differs.
- Structured output: Ben will bring a Node sample that streams tokens and emits an "action" event when the model returns a structured action object. If you have a preferred internal webhook schema, send it over and well adapt the example.

Can you confirm: preferred times for the deep-dive next week (Aug 18-20)? Also please attach any internal network diagram (VPC CIDRs, NAT gateways) if available — we reviewed the datasprout-proposed-arch.png but a clearer CIDR layout will let us propose exact SG rules.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
